title: Nor does the tradition of the first three centuries know such worship
source_text: LX. Neque solum altum est de rebus istis silentium in scriptis Novi Testamenti, sed nec ex Ecclesiastica trium primorum saeculorum traditione simile quid exsculpi potest. Non pauci fuerunt illustres per istud tempus apud Christianos scriptores, quorum monumenta supersunt, & qui in manibus hominum versantur. Quales apud Latinos Tertullianus, Cyprianus, Lactantius, & Arnobius; & apud Graecos Justinus, Athenagoras, Irenaeus, Clemens Alexandrinus, Origenes & alii complures: apud quos nullibi legitur cultum aliquem hodierno in Ecclesia Romana similem, Angelis & Sanctis mortuis, vel exhibitum olim, vel jam exhibendum esse: contrarium vero multis & manifestis admodum indiciis colligitur.
pass_a_gloss: And not only is there deep silence about those things in the writings of the New Testament, but neither can anything similar be carved out of the Ecclesiastical tradition of the first three centuries. Not a few were the illustrious writers among the Christians through that time, whose monuments survive, and which are in the hands of men. Such as among the Latins Tertullian, Cyprian, Lactantius, and Arnobius; and among the Greeks Justin, Athenagoras, Irenaeus, Clement of Alexandria, Origen and very many others: in whom it is nowhere read that any worship like that of today in the Roman Church was either shown formerly, or is now to be shown, to Angels and dead Saints: but the contrary is gathered from many and quite manifest indications.
pass_b_english: Not only is there deep silence about these things in the writings of the New Testament; nothing of the kind can be extracted from the church's tradition of the first three centuries either.

There were many distinguished Christian writers in that period whose works survive and are in people's hands: among the Latins, Tertullian, Cyprian, Lactantius, and Arnobius; among the Greeks, Justin, Athenagoras, Irenaeus, Clement of Alexandria, Origen, and many others. Nowhere in them do we read that any worship like that of the present Roman Church was once given, or is now to be given, to angels and dead saints. On the contrary, many quite obvious signs point the other way.

lemmas.gloss: are in the hands of men

choices.why: The image is of chiseling something out by force; 'extracted' keeps the sense of a forced reading.
